rfi.description: Centre-right politician Raphael Glucksmann has won France’s primary of the left to become the its candidate in next year's presidential elections, positioning himself as the centre-left’s main alternative to hard-left leader Jean-Luc Melenchon in the face of the rise of far right leader Marine Le Pen.

rfi.title: France urges Palestinians to reverse decision on delayed elections
rfi.description: France on Sunday called on Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas to reverse a decision to postpone legislative elections, originally set for 28 November. Abbas said on Saturday that due to "Israeli obstacles", the vote would be held in September next year, alongside a presidential poll.

rfi.title: Nikol Pashinyan says Armenia’s relations with Russia ‘can no longer be the same’
rfi.description: Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan has told RFI that his country intends to continue drawing closer to the European Union while maintaining ties with Russia, as Yerevan pursues what he describes as a more balanced and independent foreign policy.

rfi.title: Activists urge Senegal to halt LGBT crackdown as Youth Olympic Games near
rfi.description: Senegal should halt its crackdown on same-sex relations, which calls into question the country's compliance with the Olympic charter ahead of hosting the Youth Olympic Games, Human Rights Watch said Monday.

rfi.title: A year after Madagascar's Gen Z protests and Rajoelina’s ouster, little promised change
rfi.description: A year after Madagascar’s then-president Andry Rajoelina fled the country following more than two weeks of youth-led protests, the military-backed transition has yet to deliver on its promise of a political “refoundation”.

rfi.title: Western leaders slam Houthi attack on Riyadh airport, warn citizens to stay away
rfi.description: UN and EU leaders voiced shock and anger on Sunday following an attack by Yemen's Houthi rebels on Riyadh airport in Saudi Arabia and warned against an escalation in the deadly conflict. Several embassies have issued warnings to their citizens to avoid the area.

rfi.title: Rescuers search for missing migrants after deadly boat wreck off Djibouti
rfi.description: The death toll from a boat sinking off the shores of Djibouti on the night of 8-9 October, has risen to at least 139, a UN agency said Sunday, after 30 more bodies were found. Rescue operations are underway to find the dozens of missing. More than 80 people survived the shipwreck, all Ethiopian nationals.

rfi.title: Climate lawsuits gain ground as governments scale back climate action
rfi.description: The political fight against global warming may be losing steam, but the legal battle is heating up. Over the past decade, legal activists have successfully taken a number of national governments to court, triggering the adoption of more climate-friendly policies in countries including the Netherlands, Pakistan, Switzerland, South Korea and others.

rfi.title: How Egyptian femtech is tackling taboos around women's health
rfi.description: Cultural taboos and a lack of understanding can be a barrier for women to access healthcare in Egypt, alongside the cost of treatment. But the country's budding femtech sector is creating new pathways to help and information.

rfi.title: Palestinian Mahmoud Abu Hamda wins top photography prize at Bayeux
rfi.description: Palestinian freelancer Mahmoud Abu Hamda on Saturday won the photography category in the prestigious Bayeux award for war correspondents for his work from Gaza.

rfi.title: France boss Zidane generates 'electric atmosphere' with Nations League wins

lemonde.description: Selon des documents dont « Le Monde » a pris connaissance, la Fédération internationale de football a consenti, en 2025, à verser à la société Trump Tower Commercial LLC un loyer total de près de 4 millions de dollars sur plus de sept ans, pour le bureau « de représentation », souvent vide, de l’instance présidée par Gianni Infantino.

nzz.description: Die neuesten Meldungen aus dem Feuilleton.

nzz.title: Flucht aus dem Nationalrat – Warum immer mehr Bundespolitiker in die Kantonsregierungen wechseln
nzz.description: Immer mehr Nationalräte haben genug vom Reden und von der Gesetzgebung. Sie wollen in den Exekutiven anpacken. Vor allem in Zürich ist das Amt des Regierungsrats ein Traumjob. Eine Partei leidet besonders unter diesen Abgängen.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Krieg in der Ukraine: Unterstützung für schnellen EU-Beitritt der Ukraine sinkt +++ Putin will Deal laut Trump mehr als Selenski
nzz.description: Seit über vier Jahren führt Russland Krieg gegen die Ukraine. Die wichtigsten Entwicklungen im Überblick.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Die Nato bleibt die beste Annäherung an den «ewigen Frieden» in Europa, muss aber mehr Führung übernehmen
nzz.description: Die europäischen Staaten sollten ihre militärische Kraft weiter integrieren, damit ihre Aufrüstung nicht zur gegenseitigen Bedrohung wird. Daran hat auch die Schweiz ein existenzielles Interesse.

nzz.title: DER ANDERE BLICK - Putin will, dass Europa sich fügt. Die aussenpolitischen Vorstellungen von AfD und BSW sind bestenfalls naiv
nzz.description: Lange haben Populisten Probleme angesprochen, die andere Parteien übersehen oder ignoriert haben. Doch wenn es um die von Putin ausgehende Gefahr geht, versagt ihr Sensor.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Die Nobelpreisträgerin Navi Pillay eignet sich nicht für die Heldenverehrung – ihre Bilanz bei Frieden und Menschenrechten ist düster
nzz.description: In Pillays Amtszeit als Hochkommissarin für Menschenrechte instrumentalisierten autoritäre Staaten die Menschenrechte, Islamisten machten Jagd auf Karikaturisten, und schwere Verbrechen blieben straffrei. Mit der Übernahme des Israel-Mandats trotz BDS-Unterstützung verriet sie ihre professionelle Integrität.

nzz.title: Er lehrt sogar Ausserirdische, wie Bach klingt – Karl Richter zum 100. Geburtstag
nzz.description: Einst wurde er weltweit als führender Bach-Interpret gefeiert, dann liess die historische Aufführungspraxis seinen Stil überholt wirken. Doch das Interesse an Karl Richter ist nie erlahmt. Jetzt ist sein künstlerisches Erbe neu zu entdecken.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Die Tech-Szene diskutiert, ob KI-Modelle «Schmerzen» empfinden, wenn sie «gefoltert» werden. Das ist absurd
nzz.description: Wir dürfen KI-Modellen keine Gefühle andichten. Wer mit KI stundenlang über grausame Szenarien chattet, schadet höchstens sich selbst. Ein Plädoyer dafür, die Maschine Maschine sein zu lassen.

nzz.title: INTERVIEW - Peter V. Kunz kämpft als Tierschützer für die Feuerwerksinitiative. Er sagt: «Ich finde, die Tiere gehen vor»
nzz.description: Der bekannte Wirtschaftsrechtler ist Präsident des Schweizer Tierschutzes. Nun verteidigt er als Liberaler das Verbot von Feuerwerk.

nzz.title: Wenn Bauarbeiter lieber Autoscooter fahren: ein neuer «Sommernachtstraum» in Zürich
nzz.description: Zürichs Ballettchefin Cathy Marston zeigt im Opernhaus eine poetische Version der Shakespeare-Komödie. Neben Felix Mendelssohn sorgt unter anderem der DJ Mr Switch für musikalischen Zauber.

nzz.title: Israel und Saudiarabien: Die Allianz, die keine sein darf
nzz.description: Trotz fehlenden offiziellen Beziehungen nähern sich Israel und Saudiarabien weiter an. Wenn da nicht der 7. Oktober wäre, könnten die beiden Länder vielleicht bald einen diplomatischen Coup verkünden.

nzz.title: Bayern-Star Michael Olise: Er will doch nur spielen
nzz.description: Viele Experten halten ihn für den besten Fussballspieler der Welt, Olise könnte Ende Oktober den Ballon d’Or gewinnen. Doch der 24-jährige französische Nationalspieler tut so, als sei ihm alles egal.

nzz.title: Bei den Grünen der Achtziger Jahre finden sich weit mehr verfassungsfeindliche Parolen als bei der heutigen AfD
nzz.description: Die Befürworter eines AfD-Verbotes würden sich glücklich schätzen, könnten sie bei dieser Partei auch nur halbwegs so systemkritische Zitate finden, wie sie die Grünen bei ihrem Aufstieg darboten.

france24fr.title: Ligue des Champions : Lille tente l'ascension de la montagne Arsenal
france24fr.description: Les Lillois s’apprêtent à défier l’un des poids lourds de la Ligue des champions. Ils feront face à Arsenal mardi, finaliste sortant et référence de la Premier League. Mais entre l’envergure de l’adversaire et un projet de jeu encore en rodage, le LOSC semble loin d’avoir les armes pour créer l’exploit.

france24fr.title: En France, les émissions de gaz à effet de serre en baisse en 2026, mais le rythme reste trop lent
france24fr.description: La forte baisse de la consommation de carburants, dont les prix atteignent des sommets, ont largement participé à faire diminuer les émissions de gaz à effet de serre en France au cours des derniers mois. Selon l'organisme chargé du suivi des émissions, les rejets carbonés ont diminué de 4,1 % au premier semestre et pourraient baisser de 2,8 % sur l'ensemble de l'année.

france24fr.title: Ligue des champions : avec Lille, Olivier Giroud retrouve Arsenal
france24fr.description: Lille se déplace à Arsenal pour la deuxième journée de Ligue des champions. Olivier Giroud va retrouver son ancien club, chez qui il a passé cinq saisons et demie.

france24fr.title: Pesticides: des médecins français "haussent le non"
france24fr.description: A la Une de la presse, ce mardi 13 octobre , «l’acte V» de la mobilisation, aujourd’hui, en France, des lycéens. La confirmation, en Espagne, par le Tribunal suprême, de sa décision suspendre le droit de vote de dizaines de milliers de citoyens naturalisés. Les discussions, au sein de l’UE, sur un texte controversé, l’«Omnibus pesticides». La polémique, en France, autour d’«octobre rose». Et la course folle des physiciens pour mesurer le temps.

france24fr.title: En direct : "Une décrue par rapport aux semaines précédentes", juge le ministre de l'Éducation
france24fr.description: Estimant n'avoir reçu "que des miettes", les lycéens appellent mardi à une nouvelle journée nationale de mobilisation, alors que le gouvernement espère une décélération du mouvement à l'approche des vacances scolaires. Le ministre de l'Éducation nationale, Édouard Geffray, a jugé mardi matin que le mouvement était "plutôt sur une décrue par rapport aux semaines précédentes". Suivez notre direct.

france24fr.title: La Russie a livré pour 320 milliards de dollars d'hydrocarbures à l'Europe depuis 2022
france24fr.description: Le vice-Premier ministre russe Alexandre Novak a déclaré lundi que les pays de l'Union européenne ont acheté plus de 320 milliards de dollars d’hydrocarbures russes depuis 2022, dont 21,3 milliards au cours des neuf premiers mois de 2026, malgré les sanctions liées à la guerre en Ukraine.

france24fr.title: L'acteur RJ Mitte, qui jouait le fils de Walter White dans la série "Breaking Bad", est mort
france24fr.description: L'acteur RJ Mitte, qui incarnait Flynn, un adolescent atteint de paralysie cérébrale, comme lui, dans la série "Breaking Bad", est décédé, a annoncé son agent lundi. Il s’était engagé pour les droits des personnes handicapées.

france24fr.title: VSS : la loi intégrale, révolution ou illusion ?
france24fr.description: En France, 132 349 victimes de violences sexuelles ont été enregistrées en 2025. La grande majorité sont des femmes et près de six sur dix sont mineures. Ce mardi, les députés doivent se prononcer sur une proposition de loi qualifiée d'"intégrale" contre les violences sexistes et sexuelles. Son ambition : agir de la prévention des victimes à la condamnation des auteurs.

france24fr.title: Taxer les plus riches ? Toucher aux retraites ? La "bataille" du budget de retour à l'Assemblée
france24fr.description: Les députés commencent mardi l'examen du projet de loi de finances pour 2027. Une mission périlleuse pour Sébastien Lecornu à six mois de la présidentielle. Une motion de rejet socialiste a déjà été annoncée lundi soir.

france24fr.title: RD Congo : l'ex-président Joseph Kabila et l'AFC/M23 s'allient dans un mouvement politico-militaire
france24fr.description: L'ancien président de la RD Congo Joseph Kabila, condamné à mort par contumace pour trahison en septembre 2025, a pris la tête lundi du Front pour la refondation de la nation, une formation politico-militaire qui inclut le groupe antigouvernemental AFC/M23, soutenu par le Rwanda.

france24fr.title: Au Mondial de l'auto de Paris, les marques chinoises présentes en masse
france24fr.description: Au Mondial de l'auto de Paris, plus d'un tiers des constructeurs automobiles présents sont chinois. Ces marques représentent, aujourd'hui, 10 % des ventes dans l'Union européenne (UE). En Chine, les ventes de voiture reculent. Alors, pour écouler sa production excédentaire, Pékin s'est tournée vers l'UE. Mais Bruxelles croule sous les importations chinoises et veut protéger son marché automobile. Un accord UE-Chine a été annoncé. Il limite les importations de véhicules hybrides chinois importés

france24fr.title: Escalade : la Française Mélissa Césarone rêve des Jeux Paralympiques
france24fr.description: Pour la première fois, l'escalade sera au programme des Jeux Paralympiques de Los Angeles 2028. La Française Mélissa Césarone rêve d'obtenir sa qualification lors des prochaines compétitions internationales. La jeune athlète de 24 ans est née malvoyante et est classée en catégorie déficience visuelle. Pour grimper, elle a besoin d'un guide qui l'accompagne à chaque mouvement. Après avoir été double championne de France, Mélissa vise désormais plus haut.

france24fr.title: Au Sénégal, les élèves ont repris le chemin de l'école après une semaine d'inondations
france24fr.description: Ce lundi, au Sénégal, les élèves retrouvent enfin le chemin de l'école. Reportée à cause des inondations qui ont secoué le pays, la rentrée scolaire a finalement lieu ce 12 octobre. Alors que l'hivernage n'est pas encore terminé et que des orages et averses sont prévus dans les prochains jours, le ministère de l'Éducation a insisté sur le fait de ne pouvoir différer encore le retour en classe pour préserver le temps scolaire et le quantum horaire.

france24fr.title: Ukraine : un piège tendu par Donald Trump ?
france24fr.description: L'Ukraine est sous le choc après l'accord entre le président américain Donald Trump et son homologue russe Vladimir Poutine, qui permet à la Russie d'exporter du diesel vers les États-Unis – au risque de contourner les sanctions contre Moscou. Donald Trump annonce aussi une trêve sur les infrastructures énergétiques sans consulter Kiev, tandis que le Kremlin refuse de confirmer qu'elle est en vigueur. Sur le terrain, les frappes russes se poursuivent et font de nouvelles victimes.

france24fr.title: Enquête sur le poisson d'élevage : un drame environnemental et humain
france24fr.description: "The Outlaw Ocean Project" est un collectif de journalistes qui enquête sur des thématiques liées aux milieux marins. Leur dernière enquête porte sur les ravages de la pisciculture. Cette industrie vide les océans pour fabriquer des farines animales destinées à nourrir les poissons qui finiront dans nos assiettes. Les ressources de la pêche sont surexploitées, ce qui affame les prédateurs marins et les communautés humaines qui vivent de la pêche artisanale.

france24fr.title: À Ceuta, la visite hautement sensible du roi d'Espagne Felipe VI
france24fr.description: Le roi Felipe VI se rend mardi dans l'enclave de Ceuta, trois mois après l’arrivée de plus de 72 000 migrants en provenance du Maroc. Si cette visite se veut un geste de soutien envers la population locale, elle pourrait raviver les tensions avec Rabat qui revendique sa souveraineté sur la ville autonome ainsi que sur celle de Melilla, située à quelque 500 km.

france24fr.title: Élections de mi-mandat : le gazole russe, faux joker politique pour Donald Trump
france24fr.description: Le président américain Donald Trump a annoncé vendredi un accord avec Vladimir Poutine pour la livraison de gazole russe en plusieurs étapes. Il a ensuite annoncé, deux jours plus tard, un "cessez-le-feu énergétique" surprise entre la Russie et l’Ukraine. Le président américain veut ainsi faire baisser les prix de l’essence avant les élections de mi-mandat. Un calcul politique très risqué.

france24fr.title: En Grèce, l'ambassadrice américaine Kimberly Guilfoyle embarrasse jusqu'à Washington
france24fr.description: Nommée ambassadrice des États-Unis en Grèce malgré son parcours dans les médias et ses liens avec la famille Trump, Kimberly Guilfoyle embarrasse aujourd’hui jusqu’à Washington. Selon plusieurs médias américains, Donald Trump et Marco Rubio envisageraient de la limoger après une série de révélations compromettantes. Les précisions avec Alexia Kefalas depuis Athènes pour France 24.

zeit.title: Brände: Drei Tote bei Brand in Bochum
Kommunen: Cyberangriff legt Stadtverwaltung Eichstätt lahm
Rücktritt von Bärbel Bas: Tim Klüssendorf sieht Schwarz-Rot nicht gefährdet
zeit.description: Der SPD-Generalsekretär hat nach dem Rücktritt von Bärbel Bas keine Angst um die Koalition. Bei der Rentenreform stellt er dennoch einige Maßnahmen in Frage.

zeit.title: Umleitung: Medizinischer Notfall: Maschine landet am Flughafen Hamburg
Krieg gegen die Ukraine: Frachtschiff sinkt nach Drohnenangriff vor bulgarischer Küste
zeit.description: Ein in der Ukraine registrierter Frachter wurde im Schwarzen Meer von Drohnen attackiert. Bulgariens Regierung will den russischen Botschafter einbestellen. Das Liveblog

zeit.title: Teures Tanken und Heizöl: Inflation steigt erstmals seit Ende 2023 über drei Prozent
Inflationsrate in Deutschland: Inflation in Deutschland steigt erstmals seit 2023 über drei Prozent
zeit.description: Wegen der hohen Energiepreise ist die Inflationsrate in Deutschland im September auf 3,3 Prozent gestiegen. Das ist der höchste Stand seit Dezember 2023.

zeit.title: Lösungsorientierter Journalismus: Überall Krise? Sprechen wir mehr über Lösungen!
zeit.description: Journalisten berichten zu oft nur über Probleme, nicht auch über Auswege, findet Vordenkerin Ellen Heinrichs. Wie sich das ändern lässt und welchen Unterschied es macht.

zeit.title: Drohung im Landkreis Börde: Amoklauf in Sachsen-Anhalt angedroht – Schulen geschlossen
Einzelhandel: Insolvenzgeld für Galeria-Beschäftigte – Was folgt jetzt?
Mexikanische Pazifikküste: Tote und Vermisste nach Wirbelstürmen in Mexiko
zeit.description: In Mexiko sterben mindestens fünf Menschen, nachdem ein Wirbelsturm vom Pazifik auf das Festland traf. Ein zweiter Sturm könnte ebenfalls auf Land zusteuern.

zeit.title: Erbschaften und Schenkungen: So ungerecht vererbt Deutschland
zeit.description: Neue Daten zeigen, wie groß die Unterschiede beim Erben tatsächlich sind und welche Rolle Bildung spielt. Das aktuelle Steuersystem zementiert extreme Ungleichheiten.

zeit.title: Schwäche der Union: Gestern Germany’s Most Hated – und morgen das Kanzleramt?
zeit.description: Bei den Grünen zieht ein ungeheurer Gedanke ein: Wer gibt der Mitte Halt, wenn Union und SPD ausfallen? Hier spielt eine Partei womöglich bald auf Sieg, gezwungenermaßen.

observador.title: As notícias das 8h
observador.description: As notícias na Rádio Observador. Aconteça o que acontecer.

observador.title: Transição energética na Europa pode poupar 34.000 vidas
observador.description: Menor despesa com energia, novos empregos, melhor saúde e danos climáticos globais evitados. Recente estudo europeu elucida sobre os vários benefícios da ação climática na Europa e em Portugal.

observador.title: Inês Sousa Real faltou ao parlamento por causa do gato?
observador.description: A líder do PAN faltou à sessão no parlamento para acompanhar o seu gato Micas. O Padre Guilherme faz sucesso: está no top 100 da DJ Mag com os fones abençoados pelo Papa Francisco.

observador.title: O mundo da política já não espera por Passos Coelho?
observador.description: PSD e Chega mudaram tanto que o comboio de Passos já passou. Demissões e suspeitas de pressões no SIRESP, o MAI não tem um dia de sossego. Costa preocupa-se com casas na UE e Chega invade Coimbra.

observador.title: "Zelensky é o alvo fácil de Donald Trump"
observador.description: Francisco Pereira Coutinho defende que Trump cede a Putin e culpa Kiev para justificar os combustíveis caros. Também alerta para a vulnerabilidade da Arábia Saudita perante os ataques dos Houthis.

observador.title: Misericórdia de Alenquer abre creche onde investiu 4 milhões
observador.description: Localizada entre Alenquer e Carregado, a creche "nasce com o propósito de contribuir para uma resposta social de proximidade, acessível e ajustada às necessidades das famílias".

observador.title: FMI revê em alta crescimento do PIB português para 2,1%
observador.description: Previsões do FMI foram revistas de um crescimento de 1,7% em 2026, estimado em junho, para 2,1%, enquanto para 2027 passaram de 1,6% para 1,9%. Quanto à inflação, estima-se abrandar para 3%.

observador.title: Steve McQueen e o dueto entre Nina e Bowie que nunca existiu
observador.description: Em "66-76-26", o artista britânico cruza as interpretações do tema "Wild is the Wind", numa canção romântica contra o ruído. Uma obra sobre a vulnerabilidade, no Guggenheim até fevereiro de 2027.

observador.title: Pedro Moura toma posse como novo diretor da PSP
observador.description: Pedro Moura, que era coordenador-geral da Unidade de Coordenação de Fronteiras e Estrangeiros do Sistema de Segurança Interna, toma posse como diretor da PSP numa cerimónia presidida por Montenegro.

observador.title: Primeira visita em 20 anos de um Rei de Espanha a Ceuta
observador.description: Felipe VI, que foi proclamado Rei em 2014, vai pernoitar na cidade, pelo que será também o primeiro chefe de Estado de Espanha a dormir no enclave espanhol no norte de África desde 1927.

observador.title: Duas mãos cheias de esperança para o resto: Portugal goleia
observador.description: Portugal começou Mundial em Assunção com uma goleada frente à Suíça, com Miguel Rocha a fazer um hat-trick em cinco minutos no arranque do segundo tempo (10-0). Segue-se a Espanha, que bateu a Itália.

observador.title: O smartphone já não é só um telemóvel
observador.description: Do entretenimento à criação de conteúdos, dos telemóveis flip à expressão pessoal, o smartphone está a mudar os nossos hábitos. Ana Oliveira, da Samsung Portugal, reflete sobre esta evolução e o futuro da tecnologia.

observador.title: 7h. Montenegro/Passos: "Insucesso? Podem esperar sentados"
observador.description: Primeiro-ministro lembra que não foi desafiado nas últimas eleições do PSD e garante que o país só perdia com um acordo entre Governo e Chega. Ainda, Ferro Rodrigues critica Aguiar-Branco.

observador.title: Trump: Irão quer um acordo, mas não sabe como alcançá-lo
observador.description: Donald Trump diz que "ninguém quer ser Presidente" do Irão e que os EUA estão com dificuldades em saber com quem lidar. Ucrânia acusa Rússia de lançar mísseis balísticos contra Kiev.

observador.title: “Sabemos o nº de livros vendidos, não o de livros lidos”
observador.description: “De 22 mil palavras portuguesas, usamos no máximo 2 mil”, diz Manuel Monteiro, revisor e linguista, triste por lermos depressa, pouco e sem prazer. “Não sabemos ensinar gramática de modo atractivo”.

observador.title: Ferro acusa Aguiar-Branco de "normalizar" extrema-direita
observador.description: Socialista revela que escreveu ao atual Presidente da AR após se ter sentido "caluniado" com comentários de Ventura. Aguiar-Branco defendeu "primado da liberdade de expressão".

observador.title: MAI. Ricardo Carrilho "pressionado a cometer ilegalidades"
observador.description: Público: Dirigente do MAI acusa Neves de o pressionar para "cometer ilegalidades".  JN: Vítimas de violência vão ter de sair casa para obter licença parental a 100%

observador.title: Leão acelera (de Mercedes) para fazer história na Champions
observador.description: Nunca o Sporting venceu em França para a Champions. Os leões vão de Mercedes a casa do Lens sem o ferrari da equipa: Zalazar é baixa por lesão. Ainda, a contestação a nova derrota do Famalicão.

spiegel.title: Friedrich Merz kritisiert: »Radikale Töchter« klagt gegen Bund wegen Förderstopp
spiegel.description: Das Demokratieprojekt »Radikale Töchter« hat Kanzler Merz Rassismus vorgeworfen, dann verlor es sicher geglaubte Fördermittel. Beweisen E-Mails einen Zusammenhang? Laut der »Süddeutschen Zeitung« ist nun ein Gericht involviert.

spiegel.title: Galeria-Beschäftigte erhalten Insolvenzgeld
spiegel.description: Galeria geht durch die vierte Insolvenz in sechs Jahren, mindestens ein Drittel der Filialen wird vielleicht dichtmachen. Vorerst soll die Bundesagentur für Arbeit die Mitarbeitenden nun wohl doch bezahlen.

spiegel.title: Giftpilze erkennen: Wo tödliche Verwechslungsgefahr besteht
spiegel.description: Champignons, Pfifferlinge, Stockschwämmchen: Viele heimische Speisepilze haben giftige Doppelgänger. Eine Expertin erklärt, worauf Sie beim Sammeln achten müssen, damit Sie und Ihre Gäste das Pilzdinner überleben.

spiegel.title: Fußball: Jérôme Boateng wird Co-Trainer bei türkischem Erstligisten Trabzonspor
spiegel.description: Weil Jérôme Boateng wegen Körperverletzung verurteilt worden ist, scheiterte seine Hospitanz beim FC Bayern. Nun ist der 38-jährige Fußball-Weltmeister beim türkischen Erstligisten Trabzonspor untergekommen.

spiegel.title: Mexiko: Wirbelstürme »Simon« und »Rachel« bringen schwere Überschwemmungen
spiegel.description: Eine vierköpfige Familie und ein 71-jähriger Mann kamen ums Leben: Zwei Stürme haben in Mexiko schwere Schäden verursacht. Dutzende Menschen mussten mit Hubschraubern gerettet werden.

spiegel.title: Umfrage der Spielergewerkschaft: Fast jede zweite Fußballerin erwägt Karriereende
spiegel.description: Finanzieller Druck und psychische Belastungen lassen Fußballerinnen weltweit über ein frühzeitiges Ende ihrer Laufbahn nachdenken. Das zeigt eine Fifpro-Umfrage. Eine deutliche Verbesserung gab es hingegen auf einem anderen Gebiet.

spiegel.title: Wein in Deutschland: Weinernte wohl geringer als im Schnitt der Vorjahre
spiegel.description: Der trockene und heiße Sommer war für die deutschen Weinanbaugebiete Fluch und Segen zugleich. Das Deutsche Weininstitut rechnet mit einem krassen Einbruch, das Statistische Bundesamt ist optimistischer.

spiegel.title: Christa Pike: Notruf nach Hinrichtungsversuch wurde als Fehlalarm gewertet
spiegel.description: Die gescheiterte Hinrichtung von Christa Pike sorgt in den USA für Entsetzen, trotz zweier Giftspritzen lebte die Verurteilte weiter. Notrufprotokolle sollen nun ein weiteres Behördenversagen belegen.

spiegel.title: Digitalminister Karsten Wildberger will KI-Umsätze in Deutschland besteuern
spiegel.description: Firmen verdienen mit künstlicher Intelligenz Milliarden. Bundesminister Karsten Wildberger fordert eine Abgabe auf die Wertschöpfung und hat auch eine Idee, wofür er das Geld ausgeben würde.

spiegel.title: Quiz: Wo leuchtet welches Ampelmännchen?
spiegel.description: Das Ost-Ampelmännchen feiert seinen 65. Geburtstag und ist längst Kult. Doch inzwischen hat es Konkurrenz bekommen – von Hexen und Hasen, Luther und Marx. Wissen Sie, wo diese Figuren zu sehen sind? Machen Sie den Test.

spiegel.title: Mike Johnson: US-Repräsentantenhaus-Vorsitzender stellt sich gegen Live-Hinrichtung
spiegel.description: Das Pentagon will die Erschießung des Attentäters von Fort Hood live streamen, US-Präsident Trump stützt das Vorhaben. Doch immer mehr Republikanern sind dagegen – mit Verweis auf ungewolltes »Rekrutierungsmaterial«.

spiegel.title: Qatar Airways, Etihad Airways: Mehrere Fluggesellschaften streichen Flüge nach Saudi-Arabien
spiegel.description: Mehrere Golfstaaten-Airlines werden Saudi-Arabien in den kommenden Tagen nicht anfliegen. Zuvor hatte die Huthi-Miliz den Flughafen in Riad erneut attackiert.

spiegel.title: Bulgarien bittet EU und Nato nach Drohnenangriffen um Hilfe
spiegel.description: Im Schwarzen Meer werden zwei Schiffe angegriffen, eines sinkt, die Besatzung verschwindet. Die Ukraine macht Russland für den Angriff verantwortlich – nun bittet Bulgarien um verstärkte Ermittlungshilfe.

spiegel.title: Käufer zahlt 14 Millionen Dollar für Michael-Jordan-Trikot
spiegel.description: Wohl noch nie hat jemand für ein Basketball-Erinnerungsstück so viel bezahlt: Ein Immobilieninvestor hat ein Trikot von Michael Jordan für 14 Millionen Dollar erstanden. Damit brach er einen kürzlich aufgestellten Rekord.

spiegel.title: USA: Elon Musk soll 276 Millionen Dollar für die Republikaner gespendet haben

phys-org.description: A century of recipes published in the magazine Good Housekeeping reveals how the variety of seafood presented to U.K. readers has "narrowed," new research shows.

phys-org.title: Snakebites are a far bigger problem than we knew: new study maps the hidden dangers
phys-org.description: Not every snakebite injects venom. When venom enters the body, however, it can cause snake envenoming. This is a potentially fatal condition that mostly affects poor rural communities across tropical and subtropical regions where people don't have easy access to medical care.

phys-org.title: Stabilizing a simple amino acid opens a path to biodegradable sensors
phys-org.description: The humble amino acid glycine—the simplest of all amino acids—is everywhere. The human body produces it, and it helps make up our skin, bones and ligaments. It's found in meats like beef and has even been discovered in comets returned from outer space.

phys-org.title: Gravity and quantum information linked through a derivation of Einstein's equations
phys-org.description: Recent research shows that gravity and quantum information are deeply connected and that the shape of spacetime can be traced back to the way information is stored in quantum fields.

phys-org.title: New research traces the origins and human impact of Britain's largest medieval lead industry through ancient teeth
phys-org.description: The first definitive evidence of when post-Roman lead production began in one of Europe's largest medieval lead-producing regions, the Derbyshire Peak District in central England, has been uncovered by archaeologists after centuries of mining had erased much of the archaeological evidence. The work has been published in Antiquity.

phys-org.title: Magnetic sculpting transforms single-source fields into predetermined shapes with mathematical precision
phys-org.description: Magnetic fields are invisible yet essential components in technologies ranging from MRI scanners and particle accelerators to atomic clocks and future quantum computers. Each of these applications requires magnetic fields with specific shapes and properties. Today, creating such tailored magnetic fields requires researchers and engineers to design specialized, carefully optimized magnets or large systems of coils for each individual application—a complex and resource-intensive process.

phys-org.title: Bacterial antiviral defense suggests ancient link to human chromosome protection
phys-org.description: A new antiviral defense system discovered by Columbia scientists could be adapted in the future into a gene editor that slows down aging in our cells and improves cancer therapies. At the same time, the discovery also sheds light on an ancient event in evolution that may have helped set the stage for the emergence of higher organisms.

phys-org.title: Electoral integrity under pressure as elections faced persistent threats in 2025
phys-org.description: Elections across the world faced a wide range of pressures on electoral integrity in 2025, from violence and misinformation and disinformation to electoral management malfunctions, cyberattacks and natural hazards, according to a new report.

phys-org.title: Nanostructure-assisted ultrasound shows potential for Parkinson's treatment
phys-org.description: Parkinson's disease (PD) is one of the most common neurological disorders associated with later life, and its prevalence rises sharply with age. It affects the brain systems that control movement, often causing tremor, stiffness, slowness and problems with balance, all of which can reduce independence and quality of life in older adults. The condition is mainly linked to the gradual loss of dopamine-producing nerve cells.

phys-org.title: Chemical disorder gives new ceramic film magnetic properties for potential low-power electronics
phys-org.description: A material thinner than a human hair may foster faster computing devices that demand less energy and store more data, according to a multi-institutional team led by researchers in the Penn State College of Earth and Mineral Sciences.

phys-org.title: From nonmagnetic to magnetic: A 2D semiconductor with electrically tunable magnetism
phys-org.description: Researchers from the National University of Singapore (NUS), in collaboration with scientists from institutions in Switzerland, the Czech Republic and Germany, have demonstrated a way to introduce magnetism into an otherwise nonmagnetic two-dimensional (2D) semiconductor and subsequently control its magnetic properties using an electrical voltage. The findings, published in Science Advances, establish a new platform for investigating electrically controllable magnetism in atomically thin materia

phys-org.title: Data-driven cricket ratings could reveal undervalued batters and bowlers through peer comparisons
phys-org.description: An analytical method could help high-level cricket franchises make more informed decisions about player recruitment, retention and team selection, according to research published in the International Journal of Services and Operations Management. The approach uses data envelopment analysis (DEA) to compare efficiency using multiple inputs and outputs. In the world of cricket, this means assessing players against their peers rather than relying on individual statistics.

phys-org.title: Reinforced vertebrae allow plunge-diving seabirds to survive high-speed impact
phys-org.description: A northern gannet scans the sea for fish from 100 feet (30 meters) in the air. Upon seeing a school, it pitches its body into a nosedive, somehow breaking the surface at 70 miles per hour (113 kilometers per hour) without breaking its neck. This daring maneuver seems to defy the laws of nature, but it's standard hunting behavior for plunge-diving seabirds.

phys-org.title: Global satellite data reveal widening recovery gap between urban and rural vegetation
phys-org.description: A global study has revealed a striking divergence in how urban and rural vegetation respond to climate stress. The study was led by Jin Wu from the School of Biological Sciences, Faculty of Science, and professor Yuyu Zhou from the Department of Geography, Faculty of Social Sciences, at The University of Hong Kong (HKU), with Dr. Zhengfei Guo as the first author.

phys-org.title: Measuring wildfire plumes to predict extreme fire behavior
phys-org.description: Predicting the unpredictable starts with understanding how extreme wildfires develop and under what conditions. This knowledge is essential to better anticipate and respond to them. To achieve this, firefighter and researcher Marc Castellnou and the GRAF/Bombers Catalonia team measure the atmosphere both inside and outside wildfire plumes.

phys-org.title: Cholesterol-linked drug boosts gene-targeting potency in early findings
phys-org.description: Nucleic acid therapeutics, such as antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs), have emerged as promising platforms for treating a variety of previously hard-to-treat diseases, including neurological diseases.

phys-org.title: Vapor-based method creates ultralight aerogels without conventional liquid-based chemistry
phys-org.description: Researchers at National Taiwan University (NTU), working across the College of Engineering, College of Medicine and National Taiwan University Hospital (NTUH), have developed a new method for producing aerogels, introducing what they describe as the world's first purely gaseous-born aerogel fabrication platform. The study is published in Nature Communications.

phys-org.title: Major cities worldwide are sinking, satellite data reveal
phys-org.description: Land subsidence is the gradual sinking of the ground, which can damage buildings, foundations, and drainage and sewage systems, and may increase flood risks. However, information on land subsidence dynamics remains limited, which makes it difficult for policymakers to identify where risks are intensifying and where urgent intervention may be needed. But the research brings up thorny ethical questions regarding animal rights and the moral status of chimeric creatures.

undark.title: AI-Driven Biology Is Only as Good as the Data Beneath It
undark.description: Opinion | The biotech and pharma industries are pouring billions of dollars into AI-driven drug discovery and development. But the genomic data used to train AI models are often incomplete, contain errors, or lack contextual information — a quality issue that threatens to slow the pace of biological research.

undark.title: In Italy, What Earth Can Tell Us About Extraterrestrial Life
undark.description: Photo Essay | From sampling hydrothermal vents and abandoned mines to lab experiments that replicate Mars’ atmosphere, scientists are using what we know about life on Earth to understand how it may exist on other worlds. Italy, it seems, provides particularly fertile ground for such explorations.

undark.title: The Evolving Quest to Build Life in a Lab
undark.description: Scientists are trying to create new life, whether to understand how biology first developed on Earth, or design new cells from scratch.  But life hasn’t happened — at least not yet. And questions around safety, as well as what even constitutes life in the first place, continue to swirl.

undark.title: The Embryos That Don’t Come From Eggs and Sperm
undark.description: Human embryo models mimic the earliest development stages; they could offer a glimpse of the first weeks of pregnancy — a mysterious period for which natural embryos are seldom available — and potentially shed light on miscarriage, congenital anomalies, and other health issues. But how far should they go?

undark.title: Book Review: A Contrarian View of How Consciousness Evolved
undark.description: In “Natural Intelligence & the Logic of Consciousness,” neuroscientist Antonio Damasio argues against the conventional theory that consciousness stems from high-level brain function and cognition, which in turn leads to feelings. Instead, he writes, our basest feelings led us to our loftiest thoughts.

undark.title: AI Presents Science with a ‘Ship of Theseus’ Problem
undark.description: Opinion | AI is being integrated into every part of the scientific process, including education, publishing, and the research itself. What does it mean if every component of the enterprise gets replaced by AI tools over time? C. Brandon Ogbunu explores what happens when science gets stripped of human involvement.

proj-syn.title: Will the Bardella Scandal Sink Le Pen?
proj-syn.description: The scandal over antisemitic comments made by the far-right National Rally's Jordan Bardella could die down quickly, enabling Marine Le Pen to stick to her current plan: win the 2027 presidential election and name Bardella her prime minister. But there are two other possible scenarios, neither of which would be good for Bardella.

proj-syn.title: Can China and America Handle Being Ordinary?
proj-syn.description: For at least a generation, China's "economic miracle" allowed its people to look at Americans not as inhabitants of a richer world, but as potential peers. But now the two societies are peers in a different sense, because the Chinese are increasingly suffering the same rude awakening that Americans did when their own miracle ended.

proj-syn.title: How to Improve Global Mineral Governance
proj-syn.description: The race to secure critical minerals has intensified at the same time as the international community has recognized the need for more sustainable and responsible mining practices. Translating the resulting frameworks and guidelines into concrete action will require consolidating Global South policy and advocacy networks.

proj-syn.title: A Global Debt Crisis Is Looming
proj-syn.description: After a decade of debt accumulation, higher interest rates and growing refinancing needs have left the global economy increasingly exposed to shocks. And now ongoing conflicts are driving up energy prices, fueling renewed inflationary pressures and revealing dangerous cracks in the existing debt architecture.

proj-syn.title: Europe Must Look Beyond the US and China to Solve Its Productivity Problem
proj-syn.description: Given America and China’s lead in AI and other cutting-edge innovations, it is not surprising that much of the European economic policy debate revolves around the need to emulate and catch up with these two technological superpowers. In fact, neither the US nor China offers a relevant or attractive model for Europe.

proj-syn.title: A Global Economic Recovery Built on Shaky Foundations
proj-syn.description: The latest update of the Brookings-FT TIGER survey reveals that global growth has stabilized, with both advanced and emerging market economies showing positive momentum. But amid persistent inflation and fiscal profligacy, policymakers will still be forced to push forward with structural reforms to unleash productivity growth.

proj-syn.title: The French Far Right Embraces Austerity
proj-syn.description: In a recent speech detailing her economic program, the French far-right leader Marine Le Pen offered what can only be described as a populist vision of fiscal consolidation. Whether she can make such a paradoxical formulation work will now determine her own future, and possibly that of Europe’s nationalist right.

proj-syn.title: Rating Africa on Its Own Terms
proj-syn.description: For decades, African countries' borrowing costs have been largely determined by major credit-rating agencies whose methods overlook key features of these economies' institutions and markets. The new Africa Credit Rating Agency could mark a turning point, challenging how the continent’s credit risk is graded and priced.

proj-syn.title: Development Finance Needs More Than One Currency
proj-syn.description: For many developing countries, renminbi-denominated loans offer a credible, increasingly accessible, and cost-effective alternative to borrowing in dollars. Now that the stability and predictability of US economic policies and institutions are in question, the Chinese currency is becoming more attractive.

proj-syn.title: Mélenchon Is Right About France’s Debt
proj-syn.description: When, in the name of moderation, centrists brand every sensible alternative to severe austerity as “nonsense,” they leave voters only one electable rebellion on offer, and the far right is happy to supply it. That is what is happening in France today.

proj-syn.title: Fukuyama, Thiel, and the Revenge of the Last Man
proj-syn.description: In his new memoir, Francis Fukuyama attempts to redeem his thesis about the end of history. But Peter Thiel’s ongoing quest to escape government oversight and wrest control of the future from democratic majorities makes a mockery of his argument all over again.

proj-syn.title: The Journalists’ Revolt Against AI Scraping
proj-syn.description: Big Tech’s oligopolistic dominance has prevented the news industry from developing a sustainable business model for the digital age—a crisis that AI is exacerbating. To preserve this important pillar of democracy, the Spanish-language publisher Editorial Perfil is suing OpenAI and Microsoft for copyright infringement.

proj-syn.title: MAGA’s Self-Destructive Culture War
proj-syn.description: Polls suggest that MAGA fanaticism might not be playing so well outside US President Donald Trump’s loyal base. But if the Democrats want to retake one or both chambers of Congress, they should concentrate on the economy and not answer Republican extremism with a culture war of their own.

proj-syn.title: How to Break the German Malaise
proj-syn.description: For too long, Germany’s political and corporate elite coasted on the country’s postwar economic and political success story, avoiding difficult but necessary reforms that could have kept extremist populist parties at bay. Now that the barbarians are at the gates, mainstream elites must rethink everything.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s Place in the Global Redivision of Labor
proj-syn.description: While the US continues to lead in software, some high-tech sectors, and hydrocarbons, China is becoming increasingly competitive in many high-tech, capital-intensive sectors, not least those once dominated by Europe. The EU does have a relative advantage in this new economic order, if only its leaders would recognize it.

proj-syn.title: The World Has Passed Peak Trump
proj-syn.description: US President Donald Trump, previously the most powerful, unpredictable force on the international stage, has now passed the peak of his ability to disrupt the international order. With his approval ratings collapsing, foreign leaders whose tenures will extend beyond his own are starting to write him off.

proj-syn.title: Global Financial Reform that Centers African Women
proj-syn.description: While gender-equality objectives often fall by the wayside in times of upheaval, the current rupture in the multilateral order creates an opportunity to build a debt architecture that will deliver for the women of Africa. The first steps toward this goal can be taken at this month’s IMF–World Bank Annual Meetings in Bangkok.

proj-syn.title: How Africa Can Leverage the US-China Thaw
proj-syn.description: As dollar borrowing costs soar, Chinese rates are approaching record lows. This divergence, combined with the US-China thaw, creates an opportunity for African governments: partner with the US on gas and with China on solar and storage, and tap lower-cost Asian capital markets to finance investments in both.

crunchbase.title: The Week’s 10 Biggest Funding Rounds: AI And Energy Top A Busy Lineup Of Large Rounds
crunchbase.description: As the AI startup boom progresses, investors appear to be leaving few niches unfunded. That was apparent in this week’s lineup of large funding rounds, which featured AI infrastructure providers, a foundational model developer, a content protection platform for the AI age, and other AI-focused startups among the top investment recipients.

crunchbase.title: Active Investors Kept Up The Deal Pace In Q3, Even As Funding Fell
crunchbase.description: Active startup investors largely kept up or increased their dealmaking pace in the third quarter, even as overall venture funding declined with the absence of new record megarounds for AI leaders.

crunchbase.title: Why Customer Workflows Are Becoming The Moat In The AI Era
crunchbase.description: AI companies can build durable moats by embedding their products in essential customer workflows, explains tech adviser Itay Sagie, who shares why founders should prioritize measurable customer dependence, while investors and acquirers should assess how integrations, trusted relationships and workflow access can strengthen retention and drive growth.

crunchbase.title: Exclusive: Gudea Lands $7M To Predict Which Online Narratives Will Go Viral
crunchbase.description: Gudea has raised $7 million in seed funding, co-led by Mudita Venture Partners and Silicon Road Ventures, to help companies anticipate which online narratives will go viral and understand who is driving them, the startup tells Crunchbase News exclusively.

crunchbase.title: Europe Posted Its Strongest Quarter In Q3 In 4 Years, As Its Venture Ecosystem Expands Beyond The UK
crunchbase.description: European startup funding reached $25 billion last quarter, well above the $14 billion invested in Q3 2025 and up slightly from the $24 billion invested in Q2. Quarterly funding was up 77% year over year, per Crunchbase data.

crunchbase.title: From Ballet To Breach Prevention: How A Magician’s Son Raised $4.2M In Seed Funding For His Cybersecurity Startup
crunchbase.description: The latest in our series of articles on venture funding to non-tech founders features a former magician's assistant and ballet dancer who's building cybersecurity software with $4.2 million in seed funding.

crunchbase.title: There Was Never An Easy AI Era, And Investors Are Raising The Bar
crunchbase.description: As AI IPOs bring greater scrutiny, argues guest author Maor Farid, founder and CEO of Leo AI, investors will increasingly prioritize customer spending growth, sustainable margins and deployment efficiency over rapid revenue growth alone.

crunchbase.title: North America’s Startup Funding Falls In Q3 As AI Giants Eye The Public Markets
crunchbase.description: In total, investors poured $92 billion into seed- through growth-stage rounds for U.S. and Canadian startups in the third quarter, per Crunchbase data. That’s a 35% decline from the prior quarter but up 50% from year-ago levels.

crunchbase.title: Crunchbase Data Shows AI’s Most Active Startups Are Becoming Serial Acquirers
crunchbase.description: Some of the AI industry’s fastest-growing startups are becoming serial acquirers, buying smaller companies to fill product gaps, enter new markets and bring specialized teams in-house, a review of Crunchbase data shows. While AI giant OpenAI is by far the busiest of these buyers, well-funded startups in legal tech, customer service and software development have also made multiple acquisitions this year.

crunchbase.title: Crunchbase Data: Q3 2026 Posted A Record Count Of Billion-Dollar Rounds As The Global AI Race Heats Up
crunchbase.description: Global venture funding totaled $159 billion in Q3 2026 with close to 6,000 startups funded, Crunchbase data shows. And while the third quarter was the lowest for startup investment so far this year, it still exceeded every other quarter since Q2 2022. We take a look at where the funding went.
